why_popular: High-concept, instantly readable premise (defuse a bomb with friends, monkey theme). It forces voice communication and chaos, which suits clips and co-op streams. Free demo during Next Fest with very low friction; it ranked #1 most-played demo on Valve's list, which created a snowball of visibility. [Qualitative, from Hypertext / Venn Studios / gg.deals coverage]
marketing_channels: Steam Next Fest June 2026 (the #1 most-played demo on Valve's list, which is ordered by unique players) [CONFIRMED – Valve list via Hypertext]; free demo kept live after the fest (6M+ players); word of mouth/co-op invites; streamer coverage likely but NOT verified; TikTok role not verified
art_style: no data (monkey/banana cartoon theme per the title and coverage; 2D vs 3D not verified)
ai_feasibility_justification: PROVISIONAL – based only on the genre description, without seeing the game. AI can: write the puzzle/module logic, Steam lobby networking boilerplate, UI and procedurally generated bomb rules (Claude Code); produce stylised cartoon assets (Meshy/Tripo for low-poly 3D or Retro Diffusion/Scenario for 2D), SFX (ElevenLabs) and music (Suno). | AI cannot: design the information asymmetry that makes communication funny, tune difficulty, playtest with real groups, or create the Next Fest momentum. A 1M-wishlist launch also needs community and server/lobby support. | Toolset: Claude Code + Godot 4 + GodotSteam (or Unity + Netcode/Fishnet with Steam lobbies), Meshy/Tripo, Retro Diffusion, ElevenLabs, Suno.

data_conflicts: Next Fest players: 675,000+ (developer) vs >1,000,000 (Venn Studios); the developer figure is used as CONFIRMED. Next Fest peak CCU: 30,000+ (developer) vs ~40,000 (secondary). Release timing: Hypertext said 15 June, mxdwn said August 2026, and Univers Simu covers a paid launch with a SteamDB record of 21,294 CCU on 2026-09-04; the release date is left unverified.
notes: PROVISIONAL: built from ONE web search, because the shared 200-call WebSearch budget ran out. That is below the spec's 3–5 searches per game. Before this record is used in the report, follow-up searches are needed for: (1) team size and country of Lefto Studio, which decides whether it fits the 1–5 person criterion; (2) exact release date and price; (3) Steam review count and % positive; (4) any confirmed unit sales; (5) engine and art style; (6) streamer/TikTok role. Lesson for a solo creator: a free, high-concept co-op demo at Next Fest can snowball (6M demo players, 1M+ wishlists), but the 21k paid-launch peak against a 30–40k demo peak shows that demo hype only partly converts to paid play.
